title: Biyaya peanut (UPL Pn 6): Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaTitle: Biyaya peanut: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaDescription: Biyaya peanut is a peanut variety from UPLB. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Biyaya is a registered peanut variety, also sold or known as UPL Pn 6. The Philippine Seed Board approved it in 1986. UPLB bred it. It takes about 101 days from sowing to harvest, with 2.09 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.text: If you came here looking for UPL Pn 6, this is the same peanut. The facts below come from the NSIC registry kept by the Bureau of Plant Industry. Compare it with the others in our [peanut variety finder](/crop-varieties/peanut), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for legumes](/land-preparation/legume-land-preparation).

items: **Days to harvest:** about 101 days from sowing to harvest.
**Yield:** 2.09 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

Biyaya peanut takes about 101 days from sowing to harvest. That is about the average of the 26 peanut varieties with a day count, 101.3 days. A shorter crop frees the field sooner and dodges more of the weather, while a longer one often fills more.

Its average yield of 2.09 t/ha beats the average of its group, 1.85. It sits in the top quarter of its group. Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
The registry gives no pest or disease ratings for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit peanut fields most often: [bacterial wilt](/diseases/bacterial-wilt), [eggplant leafhopper](/pests/eggplant-leafhopper), [Corn earworm](/pests/corn-earworm), [cutworm](/pests/cutworm), [thrips](/pests/thrips). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
Where and when to plant Biyaya peanut
Mani needs loose, well drained soil to fill its pods. Pick a variety by seed size for your buyer, and one rated against rust and leaf spot for the wet season.

items: Buy sealed packs or tagged sacks from an accredited dealer, and check the packing date and germination rate.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Try it on a small area first, beside the variety you usually plant, before you switch the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is UPL Pn 6 the same as Biyaya?
items.a: Yes. UPL Pn 6 is another name for Biyaya. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.

items.q: How long does it take to harvest?
items.a: It takes about 101 days from sowing to harvest. Then the weather and your care decide the exact day.
The record shows 2.09 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Biyaya?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
